newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoro Islands seek investment from Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Comoro Islands seek investment from Hong Kong.

text.p: The Comoro Islands are considering plans to develop a free trade zone under a scheme to attract up to 5,000 wealthy foreigners from Hong Kong to the Indian Ocean republic, Finance Minister Mohamed Ali Soilihi said in Moroni on Sunday.

The plan drawn up with a Hong Kong-based firm, Comoros International Investor Programme Ltd, aims to encourage an inflow of foreign capital to finance development, he said. But it has yet to be finally agreed upon and formally ratified by the Comoran parliament.

Documents signed by the two sides, shown to reporters, provide for registration of offshore companies. Approved individuals able to invest specific sums would receive Comoros citizenship and residence rights.

Serious economic problems in the Comoros, with a mainly Moslem population of 190,000, are partly blamed for a secessionist movement demanding a return of the islands to French rule, which ended in 1975.
